conclusions: There is a factorization K→L̃→L of α with K→L̃ an admissible monomorphism, and a dg section s:L→L̃ of L̃→L such that its associated retraction is homotopic to id on L̃.
hypotheses: (A,d) is a dg algebra and α:K→L a morphism of dg A-modules.
theorem.statement:
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
Let $\alpha : K \to L$ be a homomorphism of differential graded
$A$-modules. There exists a factorization
$$
\xymatrix{
K \ar[r]^{\tilde \alpha} \ar@/_1pc/[rr]_\alpha &
\tilde L \ar[r]^\pi & L
}
$$
in $\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\tilde \alpha$ is an admissible monomorphism (i.e. split injective on the underlying graded $A$-modules),
\item there is a morphism $s : L \to \tilde L$
such that $\pi \circ s = \text{id}_L$ and such that
$s \circ \pi$ is homotopic to $\text{id}_{\tilde L}$.
\end{enumerate}

theorem.title: Lemma — Extension

conclusions: Equivalence: every open cover of $X$ refines to a finite disjoint clopen partition of $X$ **if and only if** $X_0\to\pi_0(X)$ is bijective.
Under the additional sufficient condition both equivalent properties hold.
hypotheses: $X$ is a spectral topological space, $X_0$ its closed-point set, $\pi_0(X)$ its connected-component space.
For the *additional sufficient-condition* assertion only: $X_0$ is closed and every point of $X$ specializes to exactly one point of $X_0$.
theorem.statement:
Let $X$ be a spectral topological space; let $X_0\subseteq X$ be its closed points and let $\pi_0(X)$ denote the connected-component space. The following are equivalent:
(1) Every open cover of $X$ admits a refinement by a **finite partition** of $X$ into pairwise disjoint clopen subsets.
(2) The canonical map $X_0\to\pi_0(X)$ is bijective.
Furthermore, if $X_0$ is a closed subset of $X$ and every point of $X$ specializes to a unique point of $X_0$, then conditions (1) and (2) hold.

theorem.title: Lemma — Punctured spec

conclusions: N→N^∧_{IS} universally injective over R
hypotheses: Let R → S be a homomorphism of Noetherian rings, I ⊂ R an ideal, and N a finite S-module flat over R. For every fibre-associated prime q ∈ Ass_S(N ⊗_R κ(p)) with p=q∩R, assume IS+q≠S.
theorem.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $I \subset R$ be an ideal.
Let $R \to S$ be a ring map, and $N$ an $S$-module.

\begin{enumerate}

\item $S$ is a Noetherian ring,
\item $N$ is a finite $S$-module,
\item $N$ is flat over $R$, and
\item for any prime $\mathfrak q \subset S$ which is an associated prime of

\end{enumerate}
Then the map $N \to N^\wedge$ of $N$ into the $I$-adic completion of $N$
is universally injective as a map of $R$-modules.

theorem.title: Lemma — Ideal generated by idempotents projective

conclusions: The descent datum is effective.
hypotheses: fpqc cover and a scheme descent datum whose local structure maps are affine.
theorem.statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal U=\{S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ a family of morphisms, and $(X_i,\varphi_{ij})$ a descent datum for schemes relative to $\mathcal U$: each $X_i$ is an $S_i$-scheme, and $\varphi_{ij}:X_i\times_S S_j\overset{\sim}{\to} S_i\times_S X_j$ is an isomorphism over $S_i\times_S S_j$, satisfying the usual cocycle condition on triple overlaps. Such a datum is *effective* if it is isomorphic to the canonical descent datum $(S_i\times_S X,\mathrm{can})$ arising from some $S$-scheme $X$. If $\mathcal U$ is an fpqc covering of $S$ and each $X_i\to S_i$ is an affine morphism, then the datum is effective: there is an $S$-scheme $X$ and compatible isomorphisms $X\times_SS_i\simeq X_i$. In fact one may construct $X$ by faithfully flat descent of the quasi-coherent algebras defining the affine morphisms.

\item the closed subsets of $Y$ are the sets $f^{-1}(Z)$ for $Z \subset X$
closed.

theorem.title: Lemma — Base change unramified

conclusions: Middle system is also pro-isomorphic to a Deligne system.
hypotheses: Inverse system of bounded-coherent distinguished triangles, first and third terms pro-isomorphic to Deligne systems.
theorem.statement: For a Noetherian scheme $X$, open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and coherent bounded complex $\mathcal F^\bullet$ on $X$, choose a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$ whose vanishing set is $X\setminus U$. Define $K_n$ as the bounded coherent *subcomplex* with terms $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^q$ and differentials induced by those of $\mathcal F^\bullet$. The inverse system $(K_n)_{n\ge1}$, with maps induced by $\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F^\bullet\subseteq\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^\bullet$, is a *Deligne system* for $j$. Its restriction to $U$ is a constant system in $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$ with value $K=\mathcal F^\bullet|_U$. A *pro-isomorphism* refers to isomorphism in $\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X))$, whose Hom sets into a constant object $L$ are $\operatorname*{colim}_n\operatorname{Hom}_{D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(X)}(K_n,L)$. Let $(K_n\to L_n\to M_n\to K_n[1])_n$ be an inverse system of distinguished triangles in $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X)$ whose transition morphisms are morphisms of triangles. If the pro-objects $(K_n)$ and $(M_n)$ are each isomorphic in $\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(X))$ to a Deligne system for $U\subseteq X$, then $(L_n)$ is also pro-isomorphic to a Deligne system for this same open immersion.

theorem.title: Lemma — Determinant

conclusions: $X$ is Jacobson if and only if $|X|$ is Jacobson.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For decent $X$ and $x\in|X|$, $\kappa(x)$ is the field associated with the representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. An *elementary étale neighborhood* $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ is an étale scheme chart whose pointed field map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to X$ is such a monomorphism. Its henselian local ring is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}=\varinjlim_{(U,u)}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ over the cofiltered category of elementary étale neighborhoods, and it agrees with $\mathcal O_{U,u}^h$ for any one of them. A decent space's point-set $|X|$ is sober and admits a dense open schematic locus when it has finitely many irreducible components.

An algebraic space $X$ is *Jacobson* if it admits an étale surjective cover by Jacobson schemes. A topological space $|X|$ is Jacobson if closed points are dense in every closed subset. A *finite type point* $x\in X_{\mathrm{ft\text{-}pts}}$ is a point represented by a morphism from a field spectrum locally of finite type over $X$. A decent locally Noetherian algebraic space has a sober underlying topological space, and its specialization relations agree locally with those on elementary étale scheme charts.

 $\alpha_i : \mathcal{E}_i^\bullet \to E|_{U_i}$ in

Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. A local complete intersection (lci) ring map $A\to B$ locally factors as a smooth algebra map followed by a quotient whose kernel is generated by a regular sequence. A perfect complex is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective modules; Tor-amplitude in $[-1,0]$ means its derived tensor product with any module has cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$.

theorem.title: Lemma — Adjoint ext

conclusions: Right adjoint to proper pushforward sends normalized D_Y to normalized D_X.
hypotheses: Proper f:X→Y of finite-type S-schemes, normalized D_X,D_Y.
theorem.statement: Fix a Noetherian scheme $S$ and a dualizing complex $D_S\in D(\mathcal O_S)$. For a finite-type $S$-scheme $T$, choose a finite open covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\}$ by $S$-separated schemes, and let $p_i:U_i\to S$. Define $D_i=p_i^!D_S$, using the upper-shriek functors of separated finite-type schemes over $S$. On overlaps $U_{ij}$ their restrictions have canonical comparison isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:D_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_j|_{U_{ij}}$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. A *dualizing complex normalized relative to $D_S$ and $\mathcal U$* is a pair $(D_T,\{\alpha_i\})$ with $D_T\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ and compatible isomorphisms $\alpha_i:D_T|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_i$, such that $\alpha_j\alpha_i^{-1}=\varphi_{ij}$ on each overlap. The normalized object includes the local identifications, not merely the derived isomorphism class of $D_T$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a **proper** morphism between finite-type $S$-schemes, and let $D_X,D_Y$ be their dualizing complexes normalized relative to the same $D_S$. Let $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the right adjoint of $Rf_*$ (both schemes Noetherian and qcqs, but not necessarily separated over $S$). Then there is a canonical isomorphism $a_f(D_Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_X$, compatible with the normalization on separated open pieces.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. theorem.statement: Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. For a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, an object $D\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ is a *dualizing complex* if on every affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$ it is the sheafification of a ring-theoretic dualizing complex: a bounded coherent complex of finite injective dimension with $A\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D_A,D_A)$. theorem.title: Lemma — Affine

conclusions: Composition of right adjoints equals right adjoint to composite restriction.
hypotheses: Commutative ring maps A→B→C; derived coinduction functors typed by rings.
theorem.statement:
For a homomorphism of commutative rings $\varphi:A\to B$, let $\varphi_*:D(B)\to D(A)$ be restriction of scalars. Its right adjoint $\mathcal C_\varphi(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,K)\in D(B)$ gives $B$ its action through precomposition on the $B$-argument. In general $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(L,\mathcal C_\varphi(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(\varphi_*L,K)$. For composable ring maps $A\to B\to C$, let $\mathcal C_{B/A}:D(A)\to D(B)$, $\mathcal C_{C/B}:D(B)\to D(C)$, and $\mathcal C_{C/A}:D(A)\to D(C)$ be their derived coinduction functors $R\operatorname{Hom}$. Then the canonical natural transformation
\[
\mathcal C_{C/B}\circ\mathcal C_{B/A}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal C_{C/A}
\]
is an isomorphism; both sides are right adjoint to the same composite scalar restriction $D(C)\to D(A)$. This is an isomorphism of functors, not an untyped equality of two uses of $R\operatorname{Hom}$.

theorem.statement:
**Source terminology (not extra hypotheses).** A **w-local** spectral space has closed set of closed points and every point specializes to a unique closed point; a w-local map between such spaces is spectral and sends closed points to closed points. A ring map $A\to B$ is a **local isomorphism** when near every prime of $B$ it induces an open immersion after inverting an element of $B$; it **identifies local rings** when $A_{q\cap A}\to B_q$ is an isomorphism for every prime $q$ of $B$. A ring map is **ind-Zariski** when its target is a filtered colimit of local-isomorphism algebras over the source.

Let $A \to B$ be ring map such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A \to B$ identifies local rings,
\item the topological spaces $\Spec(B)$, $\Spec(A)$ are w-local, and
\item $\Spec(B) \to \Spec(A)$ is w-local.
\end{enumerate}
Then $A \to B$ is ind-Zariski.

Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $f : X \to S$ be a smooth morphism of schemes.
Let $\sigma : S \to X$ be a section of $f$.
Then $\sigma$ is a regular immersion.

conclusions: Refinement pullback is fully faithful, and schemes over S embed fully faithfully into descent data on an fpqc cover.
hypotheses: Both covers fpqc and U refines V.
theorem.statement: For a family $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to S\}$, let $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ be the category of families of $U_i$-schemes $V_i$ together with isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:V_i\times_SU_j\xrightarrow{\sim}U_i\times_SV_j$ over $U_i\times_SU_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. Let $\mathcal U$ and $\mathcal V$ both be fpqc coverings of $S$, and suppose $\mathcal U$ refines $\mathcal V$. Then the induced pullback $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal V)\to\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ is fully faithful. Consequently, for any fpqc covering $\mathcal U$ of $S$, the category $\operatorname{Sch}/S$ embeds fully faithfully into $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ through canonical descent data. theorem.statement:
Let $R\to A$ be finite type over Noetherian rings. The *algebraic upper shriek* $\varphi^!:D(R)\to D(A)$ is defined by a chosen surjection $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $\varphi^!(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)[n]$, with $A$-action by precomposition. For a surjection $\varphi$ this specializes to $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,K)$. It is well-defined only *up to nonunique natural isomorphism*. Its *relative dualizing complex* $\omega_{A/R}^{\bullet}$ is $\varphi^!(R)$, again up to nonunique isomorphism. A *perfect map* is pseudo-coherent and of finite Tor dimension; finite-type flat maps are perfect.

Let $\varphi : R \to A$ be a finite type map of Noetherian rings.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\varphi$ is perfect, then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\omega_{A/R}^\bullet$ is in $D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(A)$,
\item $\omega_{A/R}^\bullet$ has finite tor dimension over $R$, and
\item $A \to R\Hom_A(\omega_{A/R}^\bullet, \omega_{A/R}^\bullet)$
is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
\item If $\varphi$ is flat, then (1)(a), (1)(b), and (1)(c) hold and
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\omega_{A/R}^\bullet$ is $R$-perfect
(More on Algebra,
Definition \ref{more-algebra-definition-relatively-perfect}), and
\item for every map $R \to k$ to a field the base change
$\omega_{A/R}^\bullet \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} (A \otimes_R k)$
is a dualizing complex for $A \otimes_R k$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

**Scope and interpretation:** For perfect φ, the relative complex is bounded coherent, has finite relative Tor amplitude and the canonical homothety A→RHom_A(ω,ω) is an isomorphism. Flat φ also makes it R-perfect and its base change to every residue-field or field-valued R-point a dualizing complex on that fibre.

conclusions:
We have the following implications:
$\mathcal{J}$ is regular $\Rightarrow$
$\mathcal{J}$ is Koszul-regular $\Rightarrow$
$\mathcal{J}$ is $H_1$-regular $\Rightarrow$
$\mathcal{J}$ is quasi-regular.
hypotheses: Let $X$ be a ringed space. Let $\mathcal{J}$ be a sheaf of ideals.
theorem.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $X$ be a ringed space. Let $\mathcal{J}$ be a sheaf of ideals.
We have the following implications:
$\mathcal{J}$ is regular $\Rightarrow$
$\mathcal{J}$ is Koszul-regular $\Rightarrow$
$\mathcal{J}$ is $H_1$-regular $\Rightarrow$
$\mathcal{J}$ is quasi-regular.

A scheme map $f:X\to Y$ induces a geometric morphism $f_{\mathrm{small}}:\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute et})\to\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\acute et})$ with inverse-image functor $f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}$ (left adjoint to direct image $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$) and a ring map $f_{\mathrm{small}}^\sharp:f_{\mathrm{small}}^{-1}\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X$. A *morphism of locally ringed topoi* is a geometric morphism together with a structure-ring map inducing **local homomorphisms on all stalks**, not merely a morphism of ringed topoi. A *2-morphism* between two such morphisms is a natural transformation of inverse-image functors compatible with their structure sheaf maps; a 2-isomorphism is an invertible 2-morphism. The morphism $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$ on abelian sheaves is the direct-image right adjoint.

hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a closed immersion $j:Z\hookrightarrow X$, let $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ be its conormal sheaf. A virtual normal sheaf for $Z$ in $X$ consists of a finite locally free $\mathcal N$ on $Z$ and a specified surjection $\mathcal N^\vee\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal C_{Z/X}$. The induced closed immersion of the normal cone $C_ZX=\operatorname{Spec}_Z\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$ into the vector bundle $\operatorname{Spec}_Z\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal N^\vee)$ defines the associated completed bivariant Gysin class $c(Z\to X,\mathcal N)\in A^*(Z\to X)^\wedge$ via deformation to the normal cone. If $\mathcal N$ has constant rank $r$, this class has degree $r$. Pullback of this class along a morphism over $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{res}$; $c_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathcal E)$ means $c_{\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E}(\mathcal E)$.

A regular immersion is a closed immersion whose defining ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence; its normal sheaf is the dual of the conormal sheaf and defines a bivariant Gysin class $i^!$. A local complete intersection (lci) morphism $f:X\to Y$ admits locally a factorization as a regular immersion followed by a smooth morphism. When a global factorization $f=g\circ i$ exists with $i:X\hookrightarrow P$ a regular immersion and $g:P\to Y$ smooth, define its Gysin class $f^!=i^!\circ g^*$; it is independent of the chosen factorization. Smooth pullback $g^*$ denotes the flat bivariant class with its dimension degree.

conclusions:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The functor
$f^{-1} : \textit{Ab}(Y_\mathrm{\acute etale}) \to \textit{Ab}(X_\mathrm{\acute etale})$
is exact.
\item The functor
$f^{-1} : \Sh(Y_\mathrm{\acute etale}) \to \Sh(X_\mathrm{\acute etale})$
is exact, i.e., it commutes with finite limits and colimits, see
Categories, Definition \ref{categories-definition-exact}.
\item Let $\overline{x} \to X$ be a geometric point.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a sheaf on $Y_\mathrm{\acute etale}$.
Then there is a canonical identification
$$
(f^{-1}\mathcal{G})_{\overline{x}} = \mathcal{G}_{\overline{y}}.
$$
where $\overline{y} = f \circ \overline{x}$.
\item For any $V \to Y$ \'etale we have $f^{-1}h_V = h_{X \times_Y V}$.
\end{enumerate}
The inverse-image functor is exact on **abelian sheaves** and finite-limit/colimit exact on **set-valued sheaves**. Pullback of geometric stalks is to $ ar y=f ar x$, and inverse image of representable h_V is h_{X×_Y V}. These statements are about f_small^{-1}, not tensor pullback of modules.

conclusions: Lf^*E∈D(O_C) has Tor-amplitude [a,b].
hypotheses: f:(C,O_C)→(D,O_D) is a morphism of ringed sites.

theorem.statement:
For a ringed site (C,O), an object E∈D(O) has **Tor-amplitude in [a,b]** (integers a≤b) if H^i(E⊗^L_O F)=0 for every O-module F and every i outside [a,b]. Finite Tor dimension means such a bounded interval exists; **locally** finite Tor dimension means each object has a cover on which a finite interval exists (the interval may vary). An O-module F has Tor dimension ≤d when F[0] has Tor-amplitude in [−d,0] (source Definition tor-amplitude lines 12376–12394). The derived pullback Lf^* is contravariant on sites: for f:(C,O_C)→(D,O_D), it takes **objects on D to objects on C**. No flatness of f is required.

Let $(f, f^\sharp) : (\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \to
(\mathcal{D}, \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$
be a morphism of ringed sites.
Let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$.
If $E$ has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$,
then $Lf^*E$ has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$.

hypotheses: F is quasi-coherent on S and tau is one of the six listed topologies.
theorem.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module. Define a presheaf on schemes over $S$ by $T\xrightarrow gS\longmapsto\Gamma(T,g^*\mathcal F)$, with the natural pullback restrictions. For every $\tau$ among Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf, and fpqc, this is a sheaf for $\tau$-coverings: whenever $\{T_i\to T\}$ is such a covering, the sequence
$$0\to\Gamma(T,g^*\mathcal F)\to\prod_i\Gamma(T_i,g_i^*g^*\mathcal F)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\Gamma(T_i\times_TT_j,\mathcal F|_{T_i\times_TT_j})$$
is an equalizer.

theorem.statement:
Let $(A, \mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring. Let
$I \subset J \subset A$ be proper ideals. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A/J$ has finite tor dimension over $A/I$, and
\item $J$ is generated by a regular sequence.
\end{enumerate}
Then $I$ is generated by a regular sequence and $J/I$
is generated by a regular sequence.

conclusions: The restriction $\mathcal I^\bullet|_{\mathcal C/U}$ is K-injective over $\mathcal O_U$.

$\mathcal I^\bullet$ is a K-injective complex of $\mathcal O$-modules.
theorem.statement:
A complex $\mathcal I^\bullet$ of modules is K-injective if $\mathrm{Hom}_{K(\mathcal O)}(\mathcal A^\bullet,\mathcal I^\bullet[n])=0$ for every acyclic complex $\mathcal A^\bullet$ and every integer $n$; such complexes compute unbounded right derived functors. For $U\in\mathcal C$, the localization $j:(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C/U),\mathcal O_U)\to(\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)$ induces the exact restriction $j^*$ and exact extension by zero $j_!$. The assertion concerns **K-injective** complexes, not merely degreewise injective complexes.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $U$ be an object of
$\mathcal{C}$. The restriction of a K-injective complex of
$\mathcal{O}$-modules to $\mathcal{C}/U$ is a K-injective complex of
$\mathcal{O}_U$-modules.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.

$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules on $X$.

$$

\subset \ldots \subset \mathcal{E}_r = \mathcal{E}

theorem.title: Lemma — Orthogonal triangulated

hypotheses: A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$, put $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal F)-\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal F)$. A linear series $\mathfrak g_d^r$ is a pair $(\mathcal L,V)$ with $\deg(\mathcal L)=d$ and $V\subseteq H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ a $(r+1)$-dimensional $k$-subspace. On a nonsingular curve the image of $V\otimes_k\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is invertible, giving a morphism $\varphi_{(\mathcal L,V)}:X\to\mathbf P_k^r$ and an injection $\varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^r}(1)\hookrightarrow\mathcal L$ carrying standard coordinate sections to a chosen basis of $V$.
theorem.statement:
A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most $1$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$, put $\deg_k(\mathcal L)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\dim_kH^0(X,\mathcal F)-\dim_kH^1(X,\mathcal F)$. A linear series $\mathfrak g_d^r$ is a pair $(\mathcal L,V)$ with $\deg(\mathcal L)=d$ and $V\subseteq H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ a $(r+1)$-dimensional $k$-subspace. On a nonsingular curve the image of $V\otimes_k\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal L$ is invertible, giving a morphism $\varphi_{(\mathcal L,V)}:X\to\mathbf P_k^r$ and an injection $\varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^r}(1)\hookrightarrow\mathcal L$ carrying standard coordinate sections to a chosen basis of $V$.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a nonsingular proper curve over $k$.
Let $(\mathcal{L}, V)$ be a $\mathfrak g^1_d$ on $X$. Then the morphism
$\varphi : X \to \mathbf{P}^1_k$ associated to the pair $(\mathcal L,V)$ by the projective-space construction above
either
\begin{enumerate}
\item is nonconstant and has degree $\leq d$, or
\item factors through a closed point of $\mathbf{P}^1_k$ and in this
case $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X) \not = k$.
\end{enumerate}

theorem.title: Lemma — G1d

conclusions: The following are equivalent: every idempotent on an object of $\mathcal C$ has a kernel; every such idempotent has a cokernel; and each idempotent splits as a projection in a biproduct decomposition.
hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a preadditive category.
theorem.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a preadditive category. The following
are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{C}$ is Karoubian,
\item every idempotent endomorphism of an object of $\mathcal{C}$ has a
cokernel, and
\item given an idempotent endomorphism $p : z \to z$ of $\mathcal{C}$
there exists a direct sum decomposition $z = x \oplus y$ such
that $p$ corresponds to the projection onto $y$.
\end{enumerate}

conclusions: Étaleness of f is equivalent to étaleness of the composites.
hypotheses: An étale covering of the source of f.
theorem.statement: A property $\mathcal P$ of scheme morphisms is *étale-local on the source* if $f:X\to Y$ has $\mathcal P$ exactly when all composites $X_i\to X\to Y$ have it, for any étale covering $\{X_i\to X\}$. It is *étale-local on the target* if the corresponding equivalence holds after étale base change on $Y$. For every scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ and every étale covering $\{a_i:X_i\to X\}$, the morphism $f$ is étale if and only if each composite $f\circ a_i:X_i\to Y$ is étale.

A subset is locally constructible if its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets. An algebraic space has a locally constructible subset in the étale sense when its inverse image in every étale scheme chart is locally constructible.

conclusions:
$i$ is regular $\Leftrightarrow$

$i$ is $H_1$-regular $\Leftrightarrow$
$i$ is quasi-regular.

theorem.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion of schemes.
Assume $X$ is locally Noetherian. Then
$i$ is regular $\Leftrightarrow$
$i$ is Koszul-regular $\Leftrightarrow$
$i$ is $H_1$-regular $\Leftrightarrow$
$i$ is quasi-regular.

theorem.title: Lemma — Product representable transformations

conclusions:
a slight generalization of the above constructions
$$
c(\mathcal{E}^\bullet) \in \prod\nolimits_{p \geq 0} A^p(X),\quad
ch(\mathcal{E}^\bullet) \in
\prod\nolimits_{p \geq 0} A^p(X) \otimes \mathbf{Q},\quad

$$
are independent of the choice of the complex $\mathcal{E}^\bullet$.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a locally free $\mathcal E$ with formal Chern roots $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ (elementary symmetric polynomials equal to $c_i(\mathcal E)$), put $P_p(\mathcal E)=\sum_{j=1}^r x_j^p$, where $P_0=r$, and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\sum_{p\geq0}P_p(\mathcal E)/p!$. Each $P_p$ is the universal Newton polynomial in the Chern classes, and the degree-$p$ Chern character lies in $A^p(X)\otimes\mathbf Q$.

The derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is the localization of complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms. A perfect object is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free modules. A locally bounded complex is bounded in cohomological degrees locally on $X$; derived pullback is denoted $Lf^*$ and derived tensor product $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$.

For a bounded complex of finite locally free $\mathcal E^\bullet$, put $c(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\prod_n c(\mathcal E^n)^{(-1)^n}$ (formal multiplication and inversion in $\prod_{p\ge0}A^p(X)$), $P_p(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n P_p(\mathcal E^n)$ and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^n)$. For a locally bounded complex use this construction on open-and-closed pieces where the terms have constant rank and finitely many are nonzero. When the Chern classes of a perfect object $E$ are defined, these are the unique classes whose pullbacks to a suitable envelope agree with such a representing complex.

Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a locally free $\mathcal E$ with formal Chern roots $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ (elementary symmetric polynomials equal to $c_i(\mathcal E)$), put $P_p(\mathcal E)=\sum_{j=1}^r x_j^p$, where $P_0=r$, and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\sum_{p\geq0}P_p(\mathcal E)/p!$. Each $P_p$ is the universal Newton polynomial in the Chern classes, and the degree-$p$ Chern character lies in $A^p(X)\otimes\mathbf Q$.

The derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is the localization of complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms. A perfect object is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free modules. A locally bounded complex is bounded in cohomological degrees locally on $X$; derived pullback is denoted $Lf^*$ and derived tensor product $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$.

For a bounded complex of finite locally free $\mathcal E^\bullet$, put $c(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\prod_n c(\mathcal E^n)^{(-1)^n}$ (formal multiplication and inversion in $\prod_{p\ge0}A^p(X)$), $P_p(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n P_p(\mathcal E^n)$ and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^n)$. For a locally bounded complex use this construction on open-and-closed pieces where the terms have constant rank and finitely many are nonzero. When the Chern classes of a perfect object $E$ are defined, these are the unique classes whose pullbacks to a suitable envelope agree with such a representing complex.

Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$. Let $E \in D(\mathcal{O}_X)$
be an object such that there exists a locally bounded complex
$\mathcal{E}^\bullet$ of finite locally free $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
representing $E$. Then the characteristic-class constructions for locally bounded complexes, defined by alternating formal Chern-class products and alternating power-sum/character sums
$$
c(\mathcal{E}^\bullet) \in \prod\nolimits_{p \geq 0} A^p(X),\quad
ch(\mathcal{E}^\bullet) \in
\prod\nolimits_{p \geq 0} A^p(X) \otimes \mathbf{Q},\quad
P_p(\mathcal{E}^\bullet) \in A^p(X)
$$
are independent of the choice of the complex $\mathcal{E}^\bullet$.

\begin{enumerate}
\item an object $A$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_U)$,
\item an object $B$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_V)$, and
\item an isomorphism $c : A|_{U \cap V} \to B|_{U \cap V}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an object $F$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$
and isomorphisms $f : F|_U \to A$, $g : F|_V \to B$ such

\begin{enumerate}
\item an object $E$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$,
\item a morphism $a : A \to E|_U$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_U)$,
\item a morphism $b : B \to E|_V$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_V)$,

such that

whose restriction to $U$ is $a \circ f$

\item for every faithfully flat morphism $\Spec(B) \to \Spec(A)$

$$
\xymatrix{

\mathcal{F}(\Spec(B)) \ar@<1ex>[r] \ar@<-1ex>[r] &

}

is an equalizer diagram.

theorem.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $i : Z \to X$ be an immersion. If $Z$ and $X$ are
regular schemes, then $i$ is a regular immersion.

conclusions:
If $R$ is henselian and $A$ is a finite $R$-algebra, then $A$ is a finite
product of henselian local rings.
Every finite R-algebra A is a *finite product* of henselian local rings, not simply a ring with henselian maximal-ideal localizations in an uncontrolled infinite family.
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has objects étale $S$-schemes and jointly surjective étale coverings. The *small étale topos* is $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\acute etale})$ (sheaves of sets), and $\operatorname{Ab}(S_{\acute etale})$ consists of abelian sheaves. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\acute etale,\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ has all suitable universe-selected $S$-schemes as objects, not only étale ones. A site/topos has *enough points* when a family of its point-stalk functors detects isomorphisms of sheaves. This property is **not** a classification of all points.

A **henselian local ring** $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ is a local ring satisfying Hensel's lifting criterion: for each **monic** $f\in R[T]$ and each simple root $\bar a\in\kappa$ of $\bar f$, there is a root $a\in R$ reducing to $\bar a$. A local ring is **strictly henselian** if henselian with separably closed residue field. A finite $R$-algebra is a ring $A$ finite as an $R$-module. The *henselization* $R^h$ is a flat local ind-étale $R$-algebra henselian with residue field $\kappa$; given a **chosen separable closure** $\kappa^{sep}$, the *strict henselization* $R^{sh}$ is a flat local ind-étale algebra with separably closed residue field $\kappa^{sep}$.

conclusions: The intersection $\bigcap Z_r$ is empty.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type, quasi-coherent

theorem.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite type, quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_S$-module. The closed subschemes
$$
S = Z_{-1} \supset Z_0 \supset Z_1 \supset Z_2 \ldots
$$
defined by the Fitting ideals of $\mathcal{F}$ have the following
properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item The intersection $\bigcap Z_r$ is empty.
\item The functor $(\Sch/S)^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ defined by the rule
$$
T \longmapsto
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
\{*\} & \text{if }\mathcal{F}_T\text{ is locally generated by }
\leq r\text{ sections} \\
\emptyset & \text{otherwise}
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$
is representable by the open subscheme $S \setminus Z_r$.
\item The functor $F_r : (\Sch/S)^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ defined by the rule
$$
T \longmapsto
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
\{*\} & \text{if }\mathcal{F}_T\text{ locally free rank }r\\
\emptyset & \text{otherwise}
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$
is representable by the locally closed subscheme $Z_{r - 1} \setminus Z_r$
of $S$.
\end{enumerate}
If $\mathcal{F}$ is of finite presentation, then
$Z_r \to S$, $S \setminus Z_r \to S$, and $Z_{r - 1} \setminus Z_r \to S$
are of finite presentation.
Here $\mathcal F_T$ denotes pullback along $T\to S$.

theorem.title: Lemma — Locally free rank r pullback

conclusions: $i$ is a regular immersion.
hypotheses:
Let
$$
\xymatrix{
Y \ar[rd] \ar[rr]_i & & X \ar[ld] \\
& S
}
$$
be a commutative diagram of morphisms of schemes.
Assume that $Y \to S$ is smooth, $X \to S$ smooth, and
$i$ an immersion.
theorem.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
Y \ar[rd] \ar[rr]_i & & X \ar[ld] \\
& S
}
$$
be a commutative diagram of morphisms of schemes.
Assume that $Y \to S$ is smooth, $X \to S$ smooth, and
$i$ an immersion. Then $i$ is a regular immersion.

theorem.title: Lemma — Rf upper shriek for quasi finite

conclusions:
Let $R \to A$ be a flat finite type homomorphism of Noetherian rings.
Let $\mathfrak q \subset A$ be a prime ideal lying over
$\mathfrak p \subset R$. Then
$$
H^i(\omega_{A/R}^\bullet)_\mathfrak q \not = 0
\Rightarrow - d \leq i \leq 0
$$
where $d$ is the dimension of the fibre of $\Spec(A) \to \Spec(R)$
over $\mathfrak p$ at the point $\mathfrak q$. If all fibres of
$\Spec(A) \to \Spec(R)$ have dimension $\leq d$, then
$\omega_{A/R}^\bullet$ has tor amplitude in $[-d, 0]$
as a complex of $R$-modules.
For the first bound d is the *local fibre dimension at q*. The uniform fibre-dimension bound in the second sentence is a separate hypothesis; relative Tor amplitude [-d,0] means derived tensor with any R-module has cohomology only in those degrees.

Its *relative dualizing complex* $\omega_{A/R}^{\bullet}$ is $\varphi^!(R)$, again up to nonunique isomorphism. theorem.title: Lemma — Covering

conclusions: The Gysin morphisms form a chain map with respect to the de Rham differential.

theorem.statement:

by the local cohomology/Čech class represented by $\widetilde\omega\wedge df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge df_c/(f_1\cdots f_c)$, for a lift $\widetilde\omega$ of $\omega$. Then the Gysin maps commute with the de Rham differentials:
$$d\circ\gamma^p_{f_1,\ldots,f_c}=\gamma^{p+1}_{f_1,\ldots,f_c}\circ d.$$

theorem.title: Lemma — Lim finite projective gives finite projective

conclusions: Dimension function for quotient dualizing equals restriction of δ for A.
hypotheses: Noetherian A with dualizing ω_A; surjective A→B; induced ω_B.
theorem.statement:
Let $A$ be Noetherian with a dualizing complex $\omega_A^\bullet$. At each $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A$ let $\delta_\omega(\mathfrak p)$ be the unique integer such that the stalk-localization $\omega_{A,\mathfrak p}^\bullet[-\delta_\omega(\mathfrak p)]$ is normalized over $A_{\mathfrak p}$, meaning its derived Hom from $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is $\kappa(\mathfrak p)[0]$. This is a *dimension function*: across an immediate specialization $\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak q$ of height-one difference, $\delta_\omega(\mathfrak p)=\delta_\omega(\mathfrak q)+1$. Suppose $\varphi:A\twoheadrightarrow B=A/I$ is a surjective homomorphism of Noetherian rings, and choose $\omega_B^\bullet=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,\omega_A^\bullet)$ as the induced dualizing complex over $B$. Then the induced dimension functions satisfy
\[
\delta_{\omega_B^\bullet}(\mathfrak q)=\delta_{\omega_A^\bullet}(\varphi^{-1}\mathfrak q)
\qquad(\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}B).
\]
The isomorphism is the restriction of the numerical function under the closed immersion $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$.

hypotheses:

For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let $\mathcal{J} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$

$\mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{J}$. The following are equivalent

$\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$,
\item $\mathcal{J}_x$ is generated by a Koszul-regular sequence in
$\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$,
\item $\mathcal{J}_x$ is generated by an $H_1$-regular sequence in
$\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$,
\item $\mathcal{J}_x$ is generated by a quasi-regular sequence in
$\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$,

that $\mathcal{J}|_U = \widetilde{I}$ and $I$ is generated by a
regular sequence in $A$, and

that $\mathcal{J}|_U = \widetilde{I}$ and $I$ is generated by a
Koszul-regular sequence in $A$, and
\item there exists an affine neighbourhood $U = \Spec(A)$ of $x$ such
that $\mathcal{J}|_U = \widetilde{I}$ and $I$ is generated by an
$H_1$-regular sequence in $A$, and

that $\mathcal{J}|_U = \widetilde{I}$ and $I$ is generated by a
quasi-regular sequence in $A$,

is regular, and
\item there exists a neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that $\mathcal{J}|_U$
is Koszul-regular, and

For a site object U, j_{U!}O_U is extension by zero from the ringed slice, and its representability relates Hom to derived sections over U. The site hypotheses are exactly (i) quasi-compact **final object X**, (ii) finite cofinal coverings of every quasi-compact object by quasi-compact objects, (iii) quasi-compact pairwise fibre products inside such finite covers. has a cofinal system of coverings which are finite
and consist of quasi-compact objects,

with $U$, $U_i$ quasi-compact the fibre products $U_i \times_U U_j$ are
quasi-compact.

\begin{enumerate}

any $\mathcal{O}$-module $\mathcal{F}$, then
$K$ is a compact object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
\end{enumerate}

A first-order thickening $i:(X,\mathcal O_X)\to(X',\mathcal O_{X'})$ of ringed spaces is a morphism inducing a homeomorphism of underlying spaces, a surjection $\mathcal O_{X'}\twoheadrightarrow i_*\mathcal O_X$, and a square-zero kernel $\mathcal I$. Identify the underlying topological spaces, so $\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}/\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal I$ is an $\mathcal O_X$-module. More generally a thickening only requires the kernel to be locally nilpotent.

A morphism of first-order thickenings $(f,f')$ is a commuting square of ringed spaces $(X,\mathcal O_X)\xrightarrow{i}(X',\mathcal O_{X'})$ over $(S,\mathcal O_S)\xrightarrow{t}(S',\mathcal O_{S'})$, with vertical morphisms $f:X\to S$ and $f':X'\to S'$. Put $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_{X'}\to\mathcal O_X)$ and $\mathcal J=\ker(\mathcal O_{S'}\to\mathcal O_S)$. The induced homomorphism $(f')^*\mathcal J\to\mathcal I$ equals $f^*\mathcal J\to\mathcal I$ for first-order thickenings. The morphism of thickenings is called strict if this map is surjective.

Let $(f, f')$ be a morphism of first order thickenings in the commutative square of first-order ringed-space thickenings defined above.
Let $\mathcal{F}'$, $\mathcal{G}'$ be $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-modules and set
$\mathcal{F} = i^*\mathcal{F}'$ and $\mathcal{G} = i^*\mathcal{G}'$.
Let $\varphi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ be an $\mathcal{O}_X$-linear map.
Assume that $\mathcal{G}'$ is flat over $S'$ and that
$(f, f')$ is a strict morphism of thickenings.
The set of lifts of $\varphi$ to an $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-linear map
$\varphi' : \mathcal{F}' \to \mathcal{G}'$ is, if nonempty, a principal
homogeneous space under
$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{F},
\mathcal{G} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} f^*\mathcal{J})
$$

theorem.statement:
For functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ on a ringed space, regular means successive multiplication maps on $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})$ are injective; no nonzero-final-quotient condition is imposed here. Koszul-regular means the Koszul complex has zero homology in every positive degree; $H_1$-regular means its degree-one homology vanishes; quasi-regular means, with $\mathcal J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ the ideal sheaf generated by the sequence, that $(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal J^n/\mathcal J^{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, sending $T_i$ to $f_i$ modulo $\mathcal J^2$. An ideal sheaf is of a given type if near each point of $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal O/\mathcal J)$ it admits generators of that type. For a ring regular sequence one additionally requires the final quotient nonzero. An immersion is of a given type when its defining ideal on an open where it is closed is of that type. Relative quasi/$H_1$-regular means also that its source is flat over the base. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
Y \ar[rd]_j \ar[rr]_i & & X \ar[ld] \\
& S
}
$$
be a commutative diagram of morphisms of schemes.
Assume $X \to S$ smooth, and $i$, $j$ immersions.
If $j$ is a regular (resp.\ Koszul-regular, $H_1$-regular, quasi-regular)
immersion, then so is $i$.

conclusions: The contravariant character-dual functor is exact and detects injections/surjections by reversing them.
hypotheses: $R$ is a commutative ring and $C(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(M,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$.
theorem.statement:
For a commutative ring $R$, define the contravariant $R$-module functor $C(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(M,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$, with $R$-action $(r\cdot\lambda)(m)=\lambda(rm)$. Then $C$ is an exact contravariant functor: for each short exact sequence $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ the sequence

is exact. Furthermore, it reflects monomorphisms and epimorphisms: an $R$-linear map $u:M\to N$ is injective if and only if $C(u):C(N)\to C(M)$ is surjective, and $u$ is surjective if and only if $C(u)$ is injective.

theorem.title: Lemma — ML local

conclusions: The proper relative dualizing complex with pre-rigidity is a relative dualizing pair.
hypotheses: S qcqs and f proper flat fp; omega=a_f(O_S); diagonal pre-rigidity morphism given.
theorem.statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat, locally finitely presented morphism of schemes (no quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, or Noetherian assumption). Choose an open neighbourhood $W\subseteq X\times_SX$ of the diagonal for which $\Delta:X\hookrightarrow W$ is a closed immersion, and let $p_1:W\to X$ be the first projection. A *relative dualizing complex* is a **pair** $(K,\xi)$ consisting of an $S$-perfect complex $K\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ (pseudo-coherent with locally finite relative Tor amplitude) and a *rigidifying map* $\xi:\Delta_*\mathcal O_X\to Lp_1^*K$ in $D(\mathcal O_W)$ which induces an isomorphism $\Delta_*\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_W}(\Delta_*\mathcal O_X,Lp_1^*K)$. The condition is independent of the choice of $W$ and uses the diagonal and derived internal Hom, not only self-duality of $K$. Now assume additionally $S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $f:X\to S$ *proper, flat and finitely presented*. Let $a_f$ be the right adjoint to $Rf_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories and put $\omega_{X/S}^{\bullet}=a_f(\mathcal O_S)$. Let $\Delta:X\hookrightarrow X\times_SX$ be the (closed) diagonal, $p_1$ the first projection, and $c_\Delta$ the right adjoint of $R\Delta_*$. The *pre-rigidity* isomorphism $\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}c_\Delta(Lp_1^*\omega_{X/S}^{\bullet})$ from relative duality determines, by diagonal adjunction, a rigidifying map $\xi:\Delta_*\mathcal O_X\to Lp_1^*\omega_{X/S}^{\bullet}$. Then $(\omega_{X/S}^{\bullet},\xi)$ is a relative dualizing pair as above.

theorem.title: Lemma — Strict monomorphism into filtered injective

conclusions: Restricting before or after upper shriek gives naturally isomorphic functors.
hypotheses: Noetherian S, commutative square in FTS_S, horizontal maps open immersions.
theorem.statement:
Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. For any commutative square $U\xrightarrow jX$, $V\xrightarrow{j'}Y$ with vertical arrows $g:U\to V$ and $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, where $j$ and $j'$ are open immersions and $f\circ j=j'\circ g$, there is a canonical natural isomorphism of functors
\[
j^*\circ f^!\xrightarrow{\sim}g^!\circ(j')^*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_U).
\]
The square is not required to be cartesian: the result follows from composition coherence and $j^!\cong j^*$ for open immersions.

theorem.statement:
All rings are commutative with identity and all ring maps preserve identity. On the **small étale sites** the restriction $j^{-1}:\operatorname{Ab}(X_{\acute et})\to\operatorname{Ab}(U_{\acute et})$ has an **exact left adjoint** $j_!:\operatorname{Ab}(U_{\acute et})\to\operatorname{Ab}(X_{\acute et})$, *extension by zero*, defined by sheafification of the presheaf $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{V\to U}\mathcal F(V)$ for $V$ étale over $X$. It is **not generally equal** to the set-valued left adjoint $j_!^{\mathrm{Sh}}$. For modules over a coefficient ring $\Lambda$, $j_!$ agrees on underlying abelian sheaves. The right adjoint of restriction is $j_*$, the sheaf-theoretic **direct image**. On a geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$, the stalk of $j_!\mathcal F$ is the **direct sum** over lifts $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}k\to U$ of the stalks of $\mathcal F$. For a closed immersion $i:Z\to X$, $i_*$ denotes the exact small-étale direct image.

**Standalone statement with the full source hypotheses:**
Let $j : U \to X$ be an \'etale morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ in $\textit{Ab}(U_\etale)$.
If $\overline{x} : \Spec(k) \to X$ is a geometric point of $X$, then 
$$
(j_!\mathcal{F})_{\overline{x}} =
\bigoplus\nolimits_{\overline{u} : \Spec(k) \to U,\ j(\overline{u}) =
\overline{x}} \mathcal{F}_{\bar{u}}.
$$
In particular, $j_!$ is an exact functor.

**Qualification and typing:** All quantifiers and conditions from the pinned source are retained. The stated conclusion uses the site and sheaf/module categories defined above.

theorem.title: Lemma — Right localization diagram

conclusions: Cohomology lies between negative fibre dimension and zero, with relative Tor amplitude bounded by global fibre dimension.
hypotheses: f flat in FTS_S, fibre dimension at x; a uniform bound d for the relative Tor statement.
theorem.statement:
Fix a Noetherian base $S$. Write $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ for separated schemes of finite type over $S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, choose a factorization $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ an open immersion and $\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ proper. If $a_{\bar f}$ is the right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories, define $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ as $j^*a_{\bar f}$, independently (up to canonical identifications) of the chosen compactification. For a dualizing complex $D_T$ on a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, its associated dimension function $\delta_T:T\to\mathbf Z$ assigns to $t$ the unique integer such that the stalk $D_{T,t}[-\delta_T(t)]$ is a *normalized* dualizing complex over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$, i.e. $R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{T,t}}(\kappa(t),D_{T,t}[-\delta_T(t)])\simeq\kappa(t)[0]$. For $x\in X$ above $y\in Y$, let $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ be the fibre and $\dim_x(X_y)$ its local topological dimension at $x$ (minimum dimension of neighbourhoods in the fibre). Assume $f$ is flat. If $H^i(f^!\mathcal O_Y)_x\ne0$, then
\[
-\dim_x(X_y)\le i\le0.
\]
If *every* geometric fibre of $f$ has dimension at most a fixed $d\ge0$, then $f^!\mathcal O_Y$, regarded as a complex of $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$-modules, has Tor-amplitude in $[-d,0]$ (its derived tensor with any degree-zero $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$-module has cohomology only in that range).

theorem.title: Lemma — Constructions invertible

conclusions: The sheafy trace map is an isomorphism only after applying DQ_Y in general.
hypotheses: f qcqs, E and K quasi-coherent-derived, a_f and quasi-coherator defined.
theorem.statement:
Let $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ be the unbounded derived category of complexes of $\mathcal O_T$-modules having quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves. For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, denote by $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the right adjoint to the derived pushforward $Rf_*$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,a_f(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*E,K)$ naturally in $E,K$, with unit $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to a_f Rf_*$ and counit $\operatorname{Tr}_f:Rf_*a_f\to\mathrm{id}$. This right adjoint is not in general the Grothendieck upper-shriek functor $f^!$. Let $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ and $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$. Write $DQ_Y:D(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ for the *quasi-coherator*, the right adjoint to the inclusion $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\hookrightarrow D(\mathcal O_Y)$. The canonical morphism
\[
Rf_*R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(E,a_f(K))\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_Y}(Rf_*E,K),
\]
obtained from the derived internal-Hom pushforward map followed by the adjunction counit $Rf_*a_f(K)\to K$, becomes an isomorphism *after applying $DQ_Y$ to both sides*. Without the quasi-coherator the internal-Hom map need not be an isomorphism.

A closed point $x$ of a one-dimensional locally finite type $k$-scheme $X$ is a *node* if for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ some point $\bar x$ of $X_{\bar k}$ over $x$ has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. All singularities of $X$ are *at worst nodal* if each closed point is smooth over $k$ or a node. Equivalently at a node $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for a nondegenerate binary quadratic form (whose discriminant is nonzero, including in characteristic $2$). Such curves are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_Y$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$; $Y$ remains at worst nodal. The genus of $Y$ equals that of $X$.

conclusions: Coinduction along Cartier quotient is derived tensor with conormal inverse shifted [-1].

theorem.statement:
For a homomorphism of commutative rings $\varphi:A\to B$, let $\varphi_*:D(B)\to D(A)$ be restriction of scalars. Its right adjoint $\mathcal C_\varphi(K)=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,K)\in D(B)$ gives $B$ its action through precomposition on the $B$-argument. In general $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(L,\mathcal C_\varphi(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(\varphi_*L,K)$. Suppose $R\twoheadrightarrow A=R/I$ is a surjective ring map and the ideal $I\subseteq R$ is an invertible $R$-module (equivalently, locally generated by a single nonzerodivisor). Let $L=I\otimes_RA$ be an invertible $A$-module and $N=L^{-1}=\operatorname{Hom}_A(L,A)$. Then for every $K\in D(R)$ there is a natural isomorphism in $D(A)$
\[
R\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,K)\simeq K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N[-1].
\]
The shift $[-1]$ places the unique nonzero Ext sheaf of $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,R)$ in cohomological degree $1$.

theorem.title: Lemma — Construct

conclusions: Tensor by M commutes with derived exact-support Hom under these boundedness assumptions.
hypotheses: Pseudo-coherent closed immersion; K bounded below D_QCoh; M bounded-below Tor-amplitude.
theorem.statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$. Write $R\mathcal Hom_Z(\mathcal O_Z,K)\in D(\mathcal O_Z)$ for the *exact-support right adjoint* to $Ri_*:D(\mathcal O_Z)\to D(\mathcal O_X)$, characterized by $Ri_*R\mathcal Hom_Z(\mathcal O_Z,K)\simeq R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(i_*\mathcal O_Z,K)$; affine locally for $X=\operatorname{Spec}A,Z=\operatorname{Spec}B$ it corresponds to $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,-)$ with its natural $B$-module structure. Assume $i:Z\to X$ is a pseudo-coherent closed immersion, $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$, and $M\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ has locally Tor-amplitude in $[a,\infty)$ for some integer $a$ (i.e. its derived tensor with a module has no cohomology below the indicated bound, locally). Then the canonical map induced by the counit of $(Ri_*,R\mathcal Hom_Z(\mathcal O_Z,-))$
\[
R\mathcal Hom_Z(\mathcal O_Z,K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_Z}^{\mathbf L}Li^*M
\xrightarrow{\sim}
R\mathcal Hom_Z(\mathcal O_Z,K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}M)
\]
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_Z)$.

R(f')_*(g')^*\mathcal{F}^\bullet

Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring.

theorem.title: Lemma — Quasi compact closed point

conclusions: Right adjoint commutes with restriction to quasi-compact opens on D_QCoh^+, equivalently preserves closed supports.
hypotheses: f proper qcqs with either flat finite presentation or Noetherian base.
theorem.statement: Let $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ be the unbounded derived category of complexes of $\mathcal O_T$-modules having quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves. For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, denote by $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the right adjoint to the derived pushforward $Rf_*$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,a_f(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*E,K)$ naturally in $E,K$, with unit $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to a_f Rf_*$ and counit $\operatorname{Tr}_f:Rf_*a_f\to\mathrm{id}$. This right adjoint is not in general the Grothendieck upper-shriek functor $f^!$. In the cartesian open square $U=X\times_YV\xrightarrow{j'}X$, $V\xrightarrow{j}Y$ with $V\subseteq Y$ quasi-compact open, write $f_V:U\to V$ and $a_V$ for the right adjoint of $R(f_V)_*$. The *restriction comparison* is $\rho_K:(j')^*a_f(K)\to a_V(j^*K)$, obtained from the open-immersion case of the duality base-change transformation. A complex is *supported on* a closed subset if all its cohomology sheaves vanish outside that subset. Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper and $Y$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Assume either (a) $f$ is flat and of finite presentation, or (b) $Y$ is Noetherian. Then for *each* quasi-compact open $V\subseteq Y$ and $U=f^{-1}(V)$, the comparison $\rho_K:a_f(K)|_U\to a_{f|_U}(K|_V)$ is an isomorphism for all $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$. Equivalently, for bounded-below quasi-coherent-derived $Q$ supported on $Y\setminus V$, $a_f(Q)$ is supported on $X\setminus U$. This conclusion is stated for bounded-below inputs, not automatically for the entire unbounded category.

theorem.title: Lemma — Ample positive

conclusions: The Čech tensor formula gives local cohomology and right adjunction.
hypotheses: I finitely generated with f_i generators, full subcategory of complexes with power-torsion cohomology.
theorem.statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\subseteq A$ finitely generated, and $Z=V(I)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$. Let $D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)\subseteq D(A)$ be the full triangulated subcategory of complexes whose cohomology modules are $I$-power torsion. Let $C_A(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ be the *augmented alternating Čech complex* $[A\to\bigoplus_i A_{f_i}\to\bigoplus_{i<j}A_{f_if_j}\to\cdots\to A_{f_1\cdots f_r}]$, with $A$ in degree $0$, the standard alternating restriction differentials, and all terms flat. Define $R\Gamma_Z(K)=C_A(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}K\in D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)$, the right adjoint to the inclusion $D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)\hookrightarrow D(A)$. This is local cohomology, unlike $R\Gamma_I$ above for general non-Noetherian $A$. Then the functor $R\Gamma_Z:D(A)\to D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)$ is **right adjoint** to the full inclusion $D_{\mathcal T_I}(A)\hookrightarrow D(A)$, and the displayed augmented Čech formula is a natural isomorphism for *every* $K\in D(A)$. The Čech construction and its augmentation $R\Gamma_Z(K)\to K$ are independent of the generating set in the derived category.

theorem.statement:
For a ringed site (C,O) and integer m, a complex E^bullet is **m-pseudo-coherent** if locally on every site object it admits a map from a strictly perfect complex inducing isomorphisms in H^j for j>m and a **surjection** in H^m. An object E∈D(O) is m-pseudo-coherent if any representing complex has this property (equivalently some representative; see source lines 12038–12057). Pseudo-coherent means m-pseudo-coherent for every integer m, and it does **not** imply global bounded-above without extra quasi-compactness. The three assertions must be read separately; the first additionally assumes a **final object** X in C, and the other two do not.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\mathcal{C}$ has a final object $X$ and if there exist a covering
$\{U_i \to X\}$, strictly perfect complexes $\mathcal{E}_i^\bullet$ of
$\mathcal{O}_{U_i}$-modules, and
maps $\alpha_i : \mathcal{E}_i^\bullet \to E|_{U_i}$ in
$D(\mathcal{O}_{U_i})$ with $H^j(\alpha_i)$ an isomorphism for $j > m$
and $H^m(\alpha_i)$ surjective, then $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent.
\item If $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent, then any complex of $\mathcal{O}$-modules
representing $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent.
\item If for every object $U$ of $\mathcal{C}$ there exists a covering
$\{U_i \to U\}$ such that $E|_{U_i}$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent, then
$E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent.
\end{enumerate}

theorem.title: Lemma — Characterize local ring map

hypotheses:
Let $p > 0$ be a prime number. Let $S$ be a scheme in characteristic $p$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes over $S$ .
theorem.statement:
Let $p > 0$ be a prime number. Let $S$ be a scheme in characteristic $p$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes over $S$ .
Then the diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
X \ar[d]_f \ar[r]_{F_{X/S}} & X^{(p)} \ar[d]^{f^{(p)}} \\
Y \ar[r]^{F_{Y/S}} & Y^{(p)}
}
$$
commutes.
Absolute Frobenius acts identically on points and by $a\mapsto a^p$ on functions. For $X/S$, $X^{(p)}=X\times_{S,F_S}S$, and $F_{X/S}$ is the canonical map induced by absolute Frobenius.

Equivalently at a node $\kappa(x)/k$ is separable and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\kappa(x)[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for a nondegenerate binary quadratic form (whose discriminant is nonzero, including in characteristic $2$). Such curves are Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

Its dualizing sheaf $\omega_X$ is invertible. A contraction to a stable curve means a proper morphism $c:X\to X_{\mathrm{st}}$ obtained by successively contracting rational tails and bridges and whose target has no such components.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational tail* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C\cap X'$ is a single reduced point $x$, the map $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)\to\kappa(x)$ is an isomorphism, and $g(C)=0$. The contraction of the tail is $c:X\to X'$ equal to the identity on $X'$ and collapsing $C$ to $x$ via $C\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$. It satisfies $c_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}$ and $R^1c_*\mathcal O_X=0$.

For a proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension one with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and at-worst-nodal singularities, a *rational bridge* $C\subset X$ is an integral irreducible component such that $X'$ (the scheme-theoretic closure of $X\setminus C$) is nonempty, $C$ has genus zero, and the scheme-theoretic intersection $C\cap X'$ is finite of degree two over $k'=H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$ (either two $k'$-points or a degree-two separable point). Its contraction $c:X\to Y$ collapses $C$ to a point $y$ and is obtained from the pushout $Y=X'\amalg_{C\cap X'}\operatorname{Spec}k'$. hypotheses: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

For a finite locally free sheaf $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ on $X$, its operational Chern classes are $c_j(\mathcal E)\in A^j(X)$, with $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, and total class $c(\mathcal E)=\sum_jc_j(\mathcal E)$. For an integral closed $W\subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $n$, the classes $c_j(\mathcal E|_W)\cap[W]$ in $\mathrm{CH}_{n-j}(W)$ are characterized via the projective bundle $\pi:\mathbf P(\mathcal E|_W)\to W$ with tautological quotient $\mathcal O(1)$ by $\sum_{i=0}^r(-1)^i c_1(\mathcal O(1))^i\cap\pi^*c_{r-i}=0$ with $c_0=[W]$. Extend to general cycles by sum and proper pushforward, then to Chow groups.

For a locally free $\mathcal E$ with formal Chern roots $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ (elementary symmetric polynomials equal to $c_i(\mathcal E)$), put $P_p(\mathcal E)=\sum_{j=1}^r x_j^p$, where $P_0=r$, and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\sum_{p\geq0}P_p(\mathcal E)/p!$. Each $P_p$ is the universal Newton polynomial in the Chern classes, and the degree-$p$ Chern character lies in $A^p(X)\otimes\mathbf Q$.

The derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ is the localization of complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms. A perfect object is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite locally free modules. A locally bounded complex is bounded in cohomological degrees locally on $X$; derived pullback is denoted $Lf^*$ and derived tensor product $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$.

For a bounded complex of finite locally free $\mathcal E^\bullet$, put $c(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\prod_n c(\mathcal E^n)^{(-1)^n}$ (formal multiplication and inversion in $\prod_{p\ge0}A^p(X)$), $P_p(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n P_p(\mathcal E^n)$ and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^\bullet)=\sum_n(-1)^n\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^n)$. For a locally bounded complex use this construction on open-and-closed pieces where the terms have constant rank and finitely many are nonzero. When the Chern classes of a perfect object $E$ are defined, these are the unique classes whose pullbacks to a suitable envelope agree with such a representing complex.

An envelope $f:Y\to X$ is a proper morphism such that every $x\in X$ has a preimage $y$ with $\kappa(y)\cong\kappa(x)$.
